title: Natural projection isomorphisms induce internal Hom isomorphisms
statement: Let C,D be categories, tC:C→C→C and tD:D→D→D bifunctors with parametrized right adjoints hC:Cᵒᵖ→C→C and hD:Dᵒᵖ→D→D. Let e:D→C, r:C→D, s:C→D, q:D→C have adjunctions e ⊣ s and r ⊣ q. Suppose φ(L,T): e(tD(L,rT))→tC(eL,T) is invertible for every L,T, and natural in T. Then the morphism hC(eL,N)→q(hD(L,sN)) obtained by successively transposing φ(L,hC(eL,N)) followed by evaluation is invertible. If φ is also natural in L, these morphisms are simultaneously contravariantly natural in L and covariantly natural in N. No monoidal coherence or exactness is required beyond the stated parametrized adjunctions.

proof.text: Compose the inverse tensor-Hom equivalence, precomposition by the invertible projection, the e/s adjunction, tensor-Hom in D, and the r/q adjunction. Naturality of φ and of the adjunction bijections proves naturality in every test object.

For a natural equivalence E_T:Hom(T,A)≃Hom(T,B), set f=E_A(id) and g=E_B⁻¹(id). Naturality applied to f,g yields fg=id and gf=id. Expanding E_A(id) identifies f with precisely the evaluation transpose.

Transpose the desired naturality equation successively under r/q, tensor-Hom in D, and e/s. Naturality of φ in T transports the source map to evaluation. Parametrized tensor-Hom naturality transports the map of L; ordinary naturality transports the map of N. The remaining equation is exactly naturality of φ in L followed by evaluation.
